forces.title: Supply chain uncertainty boosts warehousing opportunities
forces.description: Increased volatility in the trading environment has elevated the strategic importance of logistics expertise, creating opportunities in warehousing, inventory management, and supply chain management for logistics service providers. This increased demand for expertise and resilient operations translates into potential demand for specialized warehousing and logistics park space to manage inventory and enhance supply chain resilience effectively across Europe.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Scarcity of warehouse labour impacts logistics operations
forces.description: Labour availability remains a major challenge for the transport and logistics sector in the Netherlands, with vacancy rates for drivers and warehouse workers well above pre-pandemic levels. This scarcity of operational staff can lead to increased operational costs and reduced efficiency for tenants within warehousing and logistics parks, potentially influencing their demand for new or expanded facilities and impacting landlord-tenant dynamics.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Construction costs and bottlenecks constrain logistics development
forces.description: Rising costs for construction, renovation, and sustainability improvements, coupled with execution bottlenecks (e.g., permits), are expected to increasingly constrain logistics development in the Netherlands. These factors make new-build projects for warehousing and logistics parks more financially challenging, potentially limiting the supply of new facilities in the coming years and affecting industrial developers' investment decisions and timelines.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: Geopolitical tensions increase logistics real estate demand uncertainty
forces.description: Geopolitical tensions are increasing uncertainty around international trade, directly affecting demand for logistics real estate in the Netherlands. This global instability makes investors more cautious about acquisitions and contributes to rising vacancy rates outside traditional hotspots, influencing location decisions and overall investment in warehousing and logistics parks. The ongoing shifts in trade dynamics create a significant headwind for the sector.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: Energy transition drives demand for charging infrastructure in logistics real estate
forces.description: The energy transition is pushing logistics players towards electrification, making the availability of sufficient (scope for) charging infrastructure increasingly important for logistics real estate. This factor is gaining importance in investment and location decisions, as larger, well-located warehousing and logistics park assets equipped for electrification are expected to perform better, creating a structural shift and a tailwind for developers who can integrate these features.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: Increased European defence spending drives logistics real estate demand
forces.description: Rising defence budgets across Europe, with NATO members pledging significant increases, are driving demand for industrial and logistics infrastructure. This includes space for increased local production, higher inventories, and more resilient supply chains. The UK has already seen defence-related leasing double, indicating a strong tailwind for the industrial and logistics property sector, including for warehousing and logistics parks, across Europe in the long term.
forces.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

forces.title: Defence demand mostly build-to-own, limiting leasehold opportunities
forces.description: A significant portion of the increased defence-related demand for industrial and logistics space is expected to be delivered through build-to-own (BTO) or build-to-suit (BTS) bespoke facilities. This reflects the specialized, secure, and strategic nature of defence real estate. Consequently, not all demand translates into leased space for institutional investors and landlords, limiting direct market opportunities for warehousing and logistics parks to 20-30% of new space.
forces.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

forces.title: Domestic defence production drives demand for industrial & logistics space
forces.description: The EU's strategic shift to procure 50-60% of defence needs domestically by 2030-2035 means more local production of munitions, vehicles, and drones. This directly translates into increased demand for specialized manufacturing, assembly, storage, distribution, and testing space within industrial and logistics real estate, creating a structural tailwind for developers and operators of warehousing and logistics parks.
forces.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

forces.title: Stockpiling strategy boosts demand for secure logistics space
forces.description: NATO's defence critical supply chain roadmap and the EU Stockpiling Strategy (2025) emphasize higher inventory levels and resilience, moving away from just-in-time models for critical goods. This creates structural demand for secure, long-term leased logistics and industrial space, particularly near military bases, ports, and transport links, directly benefiting warehousing and logistics parks designed for strategic storage and distribution.
forces.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

forces.title: Defence spending impact on logistics real estate is geographically fragmented
forces.description: While defence spending is rising across Europe, its impact on the industrial and logistics property sector, including warehousing and logistics parks, is expected to be uneven. Demand will concentrate in regions with existing defence-related industrial bases, specialized infrastructure, security approvals, and R&D ecosystems, rather than being spread uniformly across the continent. This creates targeted tailwinds for specific hubs but limits broader market transformation.
forces.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

forces.title: Energy and freight disruption adversely impacts cold chain logistics
forces.description: The Middle East conflict has triggered high energy inflation and widespread supply chain disruption, particularly impacting pharmaceutical inputs. Energy price increases and air freight disruptions adversely affect Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and cold chain goods logistics. This creates headwinds for cold chain real estate, a component of warehousing and logistics parks, as operational costs for tenants may rise and supply chain reliability is challenged across Europe.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: High construction costs dampen new-build logistics activity
forces.description: Norges Bank reports that low new-build activity and high construction costs are dampening growth in the logistics sector in Norway. Many commercial building projects, including logistics facilities, are being postponed due to these elevated costs. This creates a significant headwind for the development of new warehousing and logistics parks, limiting supply expansion despite potential underlying demand and hindering overall market growth.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 1/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Near-shoring and supply chain shifts boost logistics occupier activity
forces.description: Drivers such as near-shoring, increased defence spending, and Asian businesses moving supply chains towards Europe are expected to significantly improve occupier activity in the logistics real estate sector. These shifts are enhancing the attractiveness of European locations for warehousing and logistics parks, creating a tailwind for demand and helping to stabilize vacancy levels across the continent, reflecting a structural re-evaluation of global supply chain strategies.
forces.source_title: European real estate now has real momentum as liquidity and sentiment improve

forces.title: Moderating new supply aligns with improving net absorption in logistics
forces.description: New supply in the European logistics real estate market is slowly coming down, which, combined with an expected improvement in net absorption (the difference between space leased and vacated), is set to create more favorable market dynamics for warehousing and logistics parks. This cyclical adjustment helps to stabilize vacancy levels and supports rental growth, indicating a more balanced market ahead for industrial developers and REITs in the near term.
forces.source_title: European real estate now has real momentum as liquidity and sentiment improve

forces.title: Warehouse permits decline and demand saturates post-pandemic surge
forces.description: The value of permits for commercial buildings in the Netherlands fell by over a quarter in Q1-Q3 2025, with warehouses particularly affected. After a surge in demand for logistics centres driven by online shopping during the pandemic, demand has reached a saturation point. This, coupled with geopolitical uncertainty, is keeping corporate investment subdued, posing a significant headwind for the development of new warehousing and logistics parks in the near term.
forces.source_title: Dutch construction profits rise despite stalling production

forces.title: Geopolitical uncertainty subdues corporate investment in commercial buildings
forces.description: Ongoing geopolitical uncertainty is adding another layer of caution, keeping corporate investment in commercial buildings, including warehouses, subdued in the Netherlands. This general hesitancy among corporations to commit to new investments directly impacts the demand for new warehousing and logistics park developments, contributing to the decline in permit values and creating a cyclical headwind for the real estate sector's near-term outlook.
forces.source_title: Dutch construction profits rise despite stalling production

forces.title: Elevated financing and construction costs limit commercial real estate growth
forces.description: The Dutch commercial real estate market, including warehousing and logistics parks, faces significant headwinds from elevated financing and construction costs. This directly impacts the financial feasibility of new-build investments and makes investors more cautious about acquiring older assets requiring upgrades. These higher costs limit the pace of expansion and overall trade growth in the sector, serving as a cyclical headwind that impacts profitability and development decisions.
forces.source_title: Dutch commercial real estate outlook: Growth ahead, but with limits

forces.title: Stricter sustainability requirements increase investment hurdle for older assets
forces.description: To comply with Climate Agreement targets, stricter requirements on energy efficiency, renewable energy generation, and charging infrastructure are becoming essential for commercial real estate, including warehousing and logistics parks, in the Netherlands. This makes investors more cautious about acquiring older assets that require significant, often financially unviable, upgrades. This structural change drives demand for new, green facilities while posing a headwind for existing, less sustainable properties.
forces.source_title: Dutch commercial real estate outlook: Growth ahead, but with limits

forces.title: Geopolitical uncertainties reduce logistics user demand, raising vacancies
forces.description: Current geopolitical uncertainties are reducing user demand for logistics properties in the Netherlands, leading to rising vacancy rates. This impact is particularly noticeable in regions outside established logistics hotspots, many of which were developed during the pandemic boom. This cyclical headwind is prompting a shift in investment focus towards prime, well-connected locations, impacting the overall market for warehousing and logistics parks and putting pressure on rental income.
forces.source_title: Dutch commercial real estate outlook: Growth ahead, but with limits

forces.title: Grid capacity for electric charging crucial for logistics real estate value
forces.description: The expected continued growth of electric transport means that the availability of sufficient grid capacity to enable on-site electric charging will increasingly determine the value and attractiveness of logistics real estate. This structural shift creates an upside driver for well-equipped warehousing and logistics parks, while acting as a key risk for assets lacking adequate electrical infrastructure, influencing location decisions, investment returns, and future development strategies.
forces.source_title: Dutch commercial real estate outlook: Growth ahead, but with limits

forces.title: Multimodal access, automation, and labor access drive logistics location value
forces.description: In a softening demand environment, logistics locations with multimodal accessibility, automation potential, and easier access to labour remain attractive. This structural shift highlights the importance of strategic positioning and operational efficiency for warehousing and logistics parks. Investors and developers are increasingly prioritising these factors to mitigate rising vacancy risks outside traditional hotspots and ensure long-term asset value, tenant appeal, and competitive advantage in the Dutch market.
forces.source_title: Dutch commercial real estate outlook: Growth ahead, but with limits

forces.title: REIT M&A activity signals renewed investor confidence in logistics real estate
forces.description: Despite subdued overall European real estate M&A volumes in early 2025 due to geopolitical chaos and tariff turmoil, deal announcements like Blackstone's offer for Warehouse REIT and LondonMetric's offer for Urban Logistics REIT PLC in the UK indicate renewed investor confidence. This M&A activity suggests that well-funded investors and REITs are increasingly active, perceiving value and opportunity in the warehousing and logistics parks sector, creating an upside driver for the market.
forces.source_title: Tariffs dampen European real estate M&A, but a recovery is likely

forces.title: Potential for higher interest rates could slow real estate investor demand
forces.description: While current forecasts anticipate more stable interest rates for Europe, the risk of higher financing rates cannot be fully ruled out, particularly due to rising geopolitical risks or unexpected US policy shifts. Such a development would put downward pressure on investor demand for commercial real estate, including warehousing and logistics parks, potentially slowing the recovery and acting as a key risk for the sector's growth trajectory and investment volumes in the near term.
forces.source_title: Why we're expecting a cautious recovery in Dutch commercial real estate

viewpoints.title: Logistics real estate faces caution amid rising vacancies and trade uncertainty
viewpoints.description: ING Research notes increased caution among investors in Dutch logistics real estate acquisitions. Vacancy rates have risen outside prime locations, and geopolitical tensions are creating uncertainty in international trade, directly impacting demand for logistics real estate. These factors contribute to a less robust recovery for the segment, urging investors to focus on well-located, high-quality assets to mitigate risks and maintain investment viability in warehousing and logistics parks.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Strategic location maintains Dutch logistics real estate attractiveness
viewpoints.description: Despite rising caution, ING Research maintains that the Dutch logistics real estate market remains attractive due to its strategic location and role as a transit hub. The report highlights that larger, well-located assets with sufficient charging infrastructure are expected to perform better. The energy transition is pushing logistics players towards electrification, making these factors crucial for investment and location decisions due to thin margins in warehousing and logistics parks.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: European defence push to boost logistics real estate demand by 8-20%
viewpoints.description: ING Research views defence spending as an emerging credible demand driver for Europe's industrial and logistics property sector. This push is expected to add 8-20% to logistics real estate demand in the coming years, driven by pledges to increase defence budgets, local production mandates, and increased stockpiling. While not a complete transformation, it serves as a significant tailwind amidst other market shifts for warehousing and logistics parks.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

viewpoints.title: European real estate recovery expected, logistics yields show compression
viewpoints.description: ING Research anticipates further recovery in European real estate for 2026, driven by improving liquidity, institutional capital return, and stable funding costs. While risks from elevated rates and sticky inflation remain, the macro backdrop is resilient. Logistics & Retail prime yields saw a modest 6 basis points compression in 2025, indicating improving investor sentiment and a more constructive outlook for the warehousing and logistics parks sector within commercial real estate.
viewpoints.source_title: European real estate now has real momentum as liquidity and sentiment improve

viewpoints.title: Logistics demand stabilizing in Europe with improving dynamics in 2026
viewpoints.description: ING Research expects logistics demand in Europe to stabilize in 2026, despite recent increases in vacancy levels due to tariff and macroeconomic uncertainties in 2025. The outlook suggests improving dynamics, with better tenant decision-making and an expected increase in net absorption as new supply moderates. Key drivers like near-shoring, defence spending, and Asian businesses relocating supply chains to Europe are anticipated to boost occupier activity for warehousing and logistics parks.
viewpoints.source_title: European real estate now has real momentum as liquidity and sentiment improve

viewpoints.title: Logistics real estate demand softens amid uncertainty, prime locations resilient
viewpoints.description: ING Research observes a softening in user demand for Dutch logistics properties, leading to rising vacancy rates due to current geopolitical uncertainties. This effect is concentrated in newer sites outside established hotspots. However, locations with multimodal accessibility, automation potential, and access to labor remain attractive. The availability of grid capacity for electric charging will increasingly determine value, highlighting a bifurcated market for warehousing and logistics parks with prime assets performing better.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch commercial real estate outlook: Growth ahead, but with limits

viewpoints.title: Dutch commercial real estate investment activity expected to pick up in 2025
viewpoints.description: ING Research forecasts a further pickup in investor activity within the Dutch commercial real estate market, encompassing logistics real estate, for 2025. This positive outlook is underpinned by increased expected investment returns following a 13% price decline in 2022-2023, coupled with inflation-matching rent increases. Additionally, an anticipated 1.6% Dutch economic growth and more stable interest rates are reducing risk perception and stimulating user demand and rental growth for warehousing and logistics parks.
viewpoints.source_title: Why we're expecting a cautious recovery in Dutch commercial real estate

demand_drivers.description: NATO members' commitment to raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP and EU's procurement targets drive demand for industrial and logistics space for production, storage, and distribution.
EU's push for 50-60% domestic defence procurement necessitates more local manufacturing, assembly, storage, and testing space for munitions, vehicles, and drones within logistics parks.

market_sizing.methodology: Optimistic estimate by Savills for additional industrial and logistics demand across Europe and the UK, assuming NATO members converge to a 3.5% defence spending target over seven years to 2033. This represents roughly 9-10% of the total existing industrial and logistics real estate inventory, estimated at 400 million square metres. Green Street's conservative estimate is 26 million sqm (6.5% of stock) through 2035, while AXA IM and BNP Paribas estimate 16 million sqm (4% of stock) by 2030.
market_sizing.source_firm: Savills, Green Street, AXA Investment Management, BNP Paribas Asset Management, GARBE Industrial
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

demand_drivers.description: A portion of increased defence-related industrial and logistics space demand will be met through leasehold agreements for institutional investors, representing a significant annual opportunity for warehousing and logistics parks.

new_opportunities.description: With 20-30% of new defence-related space expected to be leasehold, there's an annual opportunity for institutional investors to acquire or develop 0.5 million to 1.25 million square metres (approx. 5.4-13.5 MSF) of logistics real estate for defence tenants in Europe.

market_sizing.methodology: The annual institutional opportunity for leased industrial and logistics space from the defence sector is estimated to be 2% to 5% of total annual logistics take-up across Europe. This is derived from a total potential annual take-up from defence of 8-20% (base case 14%) of Europe's average annual logistics take-up of 25 million square metres, with 20-30% of new defence-related space expected to be leasehold rather than build-to-own.
market_sizing.source_firm: Green Street, Savills, GARBE, AXA IM Alts, ING
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…
